target_customer: Online retailers, ticketing, sports and other businesses that want customer analytics and targeted marketing
problem: Small and mid-sized businesses could not easily track and optimize the customer journey from their customer data to run better marketing campaigns.
business_model: B2B SaaS customer analytics and CRM platform

founders.name: Wojciech Gryc
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a former McKinsey consultant and Rhodes Scholar; Wikipedia adds Loran Scholar.

founders.name: Jorge Escobedo
education: PhD in theoretical physics, researched string theory
Perimeter Institute and University of Waterloo, PhD researcher
founders.background_notes: YC page lists a PhD in theoretical physics; Wikipedia names Perimeter Institute and University of Waterloo.

exit.reason: The company's own site says it joined Drop in late 2018, shut its platform down by Q2 2019 and planned to build a predictive loyalty product with Drop.

competitors.name: Custora
competitors.what: Customer analytics for ecommerce focused on retention through email campaigns

technical_complexity.rationale: Predictive customer analytics needed data integration and machine learning, which the founders' physics and consulting backgrounds could support, but it used standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Integrated customer data gave some switching cost, but rivals such as Custora, RJMetrics and KISSmetrics served the same ecommerce customers and the 2015 relaunch was described by the CEO as an expansion, not a new moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it. A loyalty company, Drop, absorbed the team and technology in November 2018.

market_need_then: In 2012 Forrester published its first customer analytics evaluation, and online retailers were adopting customer analytics, so demand for retention and targeting tools was visible. Canopy named customers from $10B retailers to sports and ticketing businesses.

branding.domain_note: Used canopylabs.com, the exact name with a labs suffix. The domain now carries the farewell notice.

identity.voice_and_tone: B2B analytics, with a plain farewell notice at the end

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch covered the 2015 relaunch and the name is real and easy to spell, but many unrelated Canopy companies share it and no community or brand driven growth was found.

pivots.from: Customer analytics and marketing for small online businesses
pivots.to: Platform mapping customers through fuzzy purchase funnels
pivots.why: CEO called it more of an expansion of the existing model than a real pivot.

outcome_analysis: Canopy Labs raised a seed of about 1.5 million dollars in December 2012 right after YC Summer 2012, then a smaller round in 2014, and relaunched its platform in March 2015 as a funnel analytics product. It never reported a large later round and joined Drop Technologies in November 2018, shutting its platform by Q2 2019 and moving its machine learning and customer success work into a loyalty product. The deal terms are not public, so the exit reads as a soft landing for a team that stayed small rather than a growth outcome.
notes: The December 2012 round is C$1.5M per PEI citing the Toronto Star, and $1.5M per Wikipedia and TechCrunch; amount_usd uses 1500000 without converting. Wikipedia calls it a seed round while one search summary called it Series A; the label seed follows PEI. The March 2014 round of about $564K rests on Seedtable only (seen via search snippet), consistent with Wellfound and CB Insights totals of about $2.1M, so coverage is partial. Investor list for the 2012 round also includes unnamed angels. The exit date is from the CB Insights and BetaKit citation of 2018-11-15, taken through Wikipedia and search results; the company's own farewell page confirms late 2018 but gives no day. A generated aggregator claiming a 2015 shutdown contradicts this and is rejected. The Custora competitor source is dated 2011-02, before the batch; its funding then is not stated. RJMetrics and KISSmetrics were seen only in undated or later pages and are excluded. Education items rest on the YC page and Wikipedia. The directory lists the company as Inactive while exit.type is acquisition because the company was acquired by Drop and its own platform was shut down.
